newsitem.title: USA: Iomega says insider sales followed "lockout.
newsitem.headline: Iomega says insider sales followed "lockout.

text.p: Iomega Corp Treasurer Robert Simmons said stock sales by insiders in the fourth quarter of 1996 were linked to a nine-month period in which they could not sell due to a company equity offering.
"You have to understand it (the insider sales) in the context of that fact that they were locked out for nine months," Simmons said at an Emerald Asset Management seminar.
He was speaking in response to an audience member's question asking to explain what the questioner said appeared to be active insider sales.
The equity offering was in June 1996 and Simmons said top executives were prevented from selling shares from November 1995 to September 1996.
Simmons also said the high-tech industry commonly uses stock incentives as part of compensation packages.
